## Summary

Demonstrate structured human goal representation and long-term experiential recall. Intent translates high-level directives ("make combat punchier") into actionable Intelligence queries. Memory tracks how assets are used, evaluated, and evolved over time.

## Prerequisite Demos

- Demo 11: Intelligence -- Assisted Decision-Making (TF-0MLXF98WZ1LQGM5W)

## New Modules

Intent, Memory

## What the User Sees

- Submit a structured intent: `toneforge intent submit --goal "reduce repetition in footstep sounds" --scope footsteps`
- Intelligence analysis produces actionable suggestions with human approval gate
- Query memory for historical context: `toneforge memory query --scope "weapon sounds" --time-range "last 30 days"`
- Memory informs intelligence recommendations via `--use-memory` flag

## New CLI Commands

- `toneforge intent submit --goal <desc> --scope <scope>`
- `toneforge memory query --scope <desc> --time-range <range>`
- `--use-memory` flag on intelligence commands

## Key Proof Points

- High-level goals translate into concrete, executable actions
- Memory prevents repeating mistakes and surfaces patterns humans miss
- Intent -> Intelligence pipeline maintains human approval at every step
- Historical data improves recommendation quality over time

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Intent submission produces an Intelligence analysis with actionable suggestions
2. No action executes without human approval
3. Memory records generation, promotion, and rejection events
4. Memory queries return time-scoped, scope-filtered reports
5. Intelligence recommendations improve when memory data is available

## Reference PRDs

INTENT_PRD.md, MEMORY_PRD.md

## Summary

Demonstrate ToneForge operating across multiple clients in sync and embedded within external tools. Network replicates behavioral events (not audio streams) for deterministic multi-client playback. Integrations show ToneForge driving sound in a CI pipeline and exporting to game engine formats.

## Prerequisite Demos

- Demo 9: Runtime & State -- Real-Time Behavioral Sound (TF-0MLXF8TBT0DJDCO1)
- Demo 12: Compiler & Validator -- Production-Ready Assets (TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD)

## New Modules

Network, Integrations

## What the User Sees

**Network (two browser windows side by side):**
- Host broadcasts state changes to connected peers
- Client receives state changes and plays deterministically identical audio
- State transitions are synchronized across all connected clients

**Integrations (CI pipeline):**
- Generate, validate, compile, and export sounds in automated pipelines
- Export for Unity/web with platform-appropriate file structure

## New CLI Commands

- `toneforge sync --target <engine> --library <path> --output <path>`
- Network API: `network.host()`, `network.join()`

## Key Proof Points

- Network sync uses behavioral events (~50 bytes each), not audio streams (~1 MB/s)
- Determinism guarantees identical playback on all clients from the same events
- CI integration enables automated sound generation, validation, and packaging
- Engine adapters map ToneForge categories to platform-specific audio groups

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Two clients play the same sound sequence from shared behavioral events
2. Network bandwidth is under 1 KB/s for typical gameplay
3. CI pipeline validates, compiles, and exports without manual intervention
4. Unity/web export produces platform-appropriate file structure
5. Late-join clients receive state snapshot and sync correctly

## Reference PRDs

NETWORK_PRD.md, INTEGRATIONS_PRD.md
data.title: Demo 15: Network & Integrations -- Distributed & Embedded

## Summary

Demonstrate publishing and consuming ToneForge assets through a marketplace. Assets are procedural systems (recipes, stacks, sequences, palettes), not static audio files -- buyers get infinite variation from a single purchase.

## Prerequisite Demos

- Demo 12: Compiler & Validator -- Production-Ready Assets (TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD)
- Demo 15: Network & Integrations -- Distributed & Embedded (TF-0MLXFBHHW1BBO1ZJ)

## New Modules

Marketplace

## What the User Sees

- Browse marketplace listings: `toneforge marketplace search --category "sci-fi weapons"`
- Install packages: `toneforge marketplace install industrial_lasers@2.1.0`
- Use installed recipes immediately with local registry
- Publish own packages with validation: `toneforge marketplace publish --package ./my-recipes/ --name "organic_footsteps" --version 1.0.0`

## New CLI Commands

- `toneforge marketplace search --category <c>`
- `toneforge marketplace install <package>@<version>`
- `toneforge marketplace publish --package <dir> --name <n> --version <v>`

## Key Proof Points

- Marketplace assets are procedural systems, not static files -- infinite variation from a single package
- Validator gates publishing -- no broken or invalid assets reach the marketplace
- Semantic versioning ensures compatibility
- Installed recipes integrate seamlessly with the local registry

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Search returns relevant packages with metadata (recipes, stacks, ratings, license)
2. Install adds recipes to the local registry and they work immediately
3. Publish validates the package before uploading
4. Installed packages maintain determinism (same seed = same output)
5. Version conflicts are detected and reported

## Reference PRDs

MARKETPLACE_PRD.md

# Tier 5 -- Character & Critter Voices

> **Goal:** Deliver the 14 character/critter voice recipes with their pages and tests,
> illustrating `classify` and `visualize`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- These 14 recipes exist as `presets/recipes/*.yaml`, validate, and appear in `toneforge list recipes`: `character-jump-voice`, `character-hurt-voice`, `character-happy-voice`, `character-effort-grunt`, `character-sigh-voice`, `creature-blob-squish`, `creature-bat-squeak`, `creature-frog-croak`, `creature-bird-chirp`, `creature-slime-bounce`, `critter-squeak-toy`, `critter-purr-soft`, `creature-ghost-whisper`, `creature-dragon-huff`.
- Each voice is distinguishable by documented pitch-register, formant/filter and envelope choices; at least four distinct techniques are represented across the tier (FM, filter sweeps, noise+tonal blends, rapid pitch modulation).
- Each recipe passes the harness battery (schema, determinism, non-silence, index presence).
- Each recipe has a page with an authored `## Sound design` section (vocal intent, register, character parameters, seed behaviour) and a generated `## ToneForge CLI` section covering `classify` and `visualize`.
- Required tags present and returned by `toneforge list recipes --tags casual`.
- Recipes render in under 1.0 s; the full suite passes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Author the 14 YAML recipes with per-character parameter signatures.
- Generate CLI blocks; author the Sound-design narratives; regenerate the index.

## Key Files

- `presets/recipes/character-jump-voice.yaml`, `presets/recipes/creature-bat-squeak.yaml` — representative tier recipes (new).
- `presets/recipes/*.yaml` — remaining tier recipes (new).
- `docs/recipe-book/*.md` — one page per tier recipe (new).
- `src/recipes/recipe-book/roster.ts` — roster entries consumed by generators/tests.
- `docs/recipe-book/index.md` — regenerated index.

## Dependencies

Blocked by **Recipe Book Harness & Tracer Slice** and **Tier 1 -- Pure Tones & Blips**.

## Deliverables

14 ToneGraph recipes; 14 book pages; regenerated index.

## Goal

Extract the preset-file discovery logic used by the golden/stack fixture
harnesses into a shared, unit-testable helper that excludes `__`-prefixed test
artefacts, so discovery can be tested in isolation and reused by both the CLI
`list` command and the fixture harnesses.

Discovered-from: TF-0MUWLVVMX003ZXVP

## Context

`src/sequence/golden-fixtures.test.ts` and `src/stack/stack-presets.test.ts`
inline `readdirSync(...).filter(f => f.endsWith(".json")).sort()`. There is no
unit-testable seam for the "ignore test artefacts" behaviour required by
TF-0MUWLVVMX003ZXVP AC #2/#3, and the CLI `list` command duplicates the same
scan in `src/cli/commands/list.ts`.

This is the **test-first/verification** child: it lands the helper and its
tests before the dependent implementation children. It does not change
`list.ts` or the fixture harnesses.

## Deliverable

- New `src/sequence/preset-discovery.ts` exporting
  `listPresetFiles(dir: string): string[]` — read all `.json` entries in `dir`,
  exclude any basename beginning with `__`, return sorted.
- New `src/sequence/preset-discovery.test.ts` unit-testing the helper.

## Key Files

- `src/sequence/preset-discovery.ts` (new)
- `src/sequence/preset-discovery.test.ts` (new)

## Acceptance Criteria

- `listPresetFiles(dir)` returns only `.json` files, sorted, excluding any
   basename beginning with `__`.
- Unit tests cover: real presets included; `__`-prefixed JSON excluded;
   non-JSON files excluded; empty directory returns `[]`; output is sorted.
- `npx vitest run src/sequence/preset-discovery.test.ts` passes.
- Tests assert observable return values, not source text.
data.title: Extract unit-testable preset-discovery helper (test-first)

data.description:
## Goal

Refactor the golden/stack fixture harnesses to discover presets through the
shared `listPresetFiles()` helper so they inherit the `__`-prefixed
test-artefact exclusion and can no longer be poisoned by a leaked fixture.

Discovered-from: TF-0MUWLVVMX003ZXVP

## Context

`src/sequence/golden-fixtures.test.ts` and `src/stack/stack-presets.test.ts`
each inline `readdirSync(dir).filter(f => f.endsWith(".json")).sort()` and
therefore register `it.each` cases for any stray JSON written into the shared
preset directories. Replace those inline scans with the shared helper from
TF-0MUYJSV32004EFAZ.

## Deliverable

- `src/sequence/golden-fixtures.test.ts` uses
  `listPresetFiles(PRESETS_DIR)` from `src/sequence/preset-discovery.ts`.
- `src/stack/stack-presets.test.ts` uses the same helper against `STACKS_DIR`.
- A regression test proves a `__`-prefixed malformed JSON present in a preset
  directory is excluded from discovery and does not produce failing cases.

## Key Files

- `src/sequence/golden-fixtures.test.ts`
- `src/stack/stack-presets.test.ts`
- `src/sequence/preset-discovery.ts` (from TF-0MUYJSV32004EFAZ)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Both fixture harnesses discover presets exclusively through
   `listPresetFiles()`; no inline `.json`/`readdirSync` filter remains in them.
- A `__`-prefixed malformed JSON placed in a preset directory produces no
   `it.each` case and no failure for the fixture harnesses.
- The existing golden/stack fixture suites still pass unchanged for real
   presets.
- Full project test suite passes (`/skill:test`, `--type full`).
data.title: Refactor golden/stack discovery onto shared helper
